_description: FINAL decoded <DWnn> redaction-token mapping for book.jsonl (RedPajama-1T book slice). The first 11.33GB is DeepMind PG19 (27,488 books), which replaced words from the Ofcom 2016 offensive-language list with <DWnn> placeholders (nn = index in their enumeration). The remaining ~96.5GB is Books3 (modern published ebooks, meta={'title'}), unfiltered. Total damage: 270,903 tokens across 20,738 books.
_provenance: PG19 README: 'mapping of offensive discriminatory words as specified by Ofcom to placeholder tokens' -> https://github.com/google-deepmind/pg19 ref [4] OfcomQRG-AOC.pdf (2016).

_mechanism.matching: case-insensitive whole-word, with plural handling (original 'negroes' -> '<DW64>s', 'darkies' -> '<DW54>s', 'pansies' -> '<DW29>s'); trailing morphology after the matched stem is preserved ('<DW37>'d' = div'd)
_mechanism.trigger_vs_replace: Books were SELECTED for filtering only if they contained strong/strongest-tier words; once selected, the FULL list (incl. medium words like coloured) was replaced. Hence 6,750 books are untouched (24.6%) and contain surviving medium words (coloured x11.7k) but essentially no strong words (slope survivors: 0).
_mechanism.case: original capitalization NOT preserved - restore heuristically (sentence-start, ALL-CAPS headings, proper nouns: Negros island, Coon Creek, Polack/Paki/Taff as names)
_mechanism.verification: 46/48 ids aligned word-by-word against modern unfiltered gutenberg.org texts (reports/originals/); remainder locked by overwhelming context + zero-survivor tests

plural_restoration.note: when token is followed by 's', restore the proper plural of the base word

ground_truth_method: reports/originals/ holds pg19_<id>.txt (corpus copy) and orig_<id>.txt (modern gutenberg.org) pairs; context-alignment votes in this session's transcript
